rubrics.criterion: The subshell-activation command in the command module (the function behind `pew workon`) no longer re-executes the shell-detection, shell-selection, per-shell rc/command preparation, PATH reconstruction, environment staging or nested-launch handling steps that the package already provides as helpers; the launch goes through calls to those existing helper functions again. Any equivalent delegation structure is acceptable as long as the private copies of those steps are gone from the command body.
rubrics.rationale: This is the deepest absorbed chain of the instance (five levels spanning the launch helpers, the process-environment helpers and raw subprocess use), and every absorbed step still has one correct, importable implementation elsewhere in the package, so the command has no reason to keep a private copy.

rubrics.criterion: The environment-creation command (the function behind `pew new`) no longer re-executes the external tool invocation with its failure cleanup, the project-association write, the PATH computation, the environment staging for installation, or the installation dispatch; it calls the existing creation, association and process helpers again, so creation/association/installation each have one implementation.
rubrics.rationale: Creation is the second absorbed chain of the instance; its expansion also re-partitioned the staging (once per installation entry), so merely moving the code verbatim does not restore the helper scheduling.

rubrics.criterion: The environment-inspection function (the function behind `pew show`) no longer performs the active-environment guard plus two captured-subprocess queries (site-packages location, interpreter version) and the installed-package inventory with inline raw subprocess wiring; it delegates to the existing captured-subprocess and inventory helpers again for both queries.
rubrics.rationale: The instance absorbed a generic captured-subprocess helper twice inside one caller with two structurally identical hand-rolled blocks; both copies must return to the shared wrapper.

rubrics.criterion: The environment-listing command (behind `pew ls` / `pew l`) no longer re-performs the environment enumeration and the terminal column arrangement inline in either output branch; it delegates to the existing listing and display helpers again for enumeration, width search, row splitting, alignment, and rendering.
rubrics.rationale: The listing path absorbed the display pipeline using the caller's own idioms (lambda instead of partial, a literal separator instead of the module constant), so the delegation must be re-established despite the rewritten surface.

rubrics.criterion: The column-printing function of the display module no longer re-implements the row splitting, width search, alignment and joining of its own module's helpers; it calls those display helpers again, restoring the module-internal layering.
rubrics.rationale: This is the second module the instance spans; leaving it expanded keeps the display pipeline implemented twice inside the very module that owns it.

rubrics.criterion: No function of the package retains a private re-implementation of the absorbed helper steps after the repair: no partially extracted leftover on some branch (for example one shell family's rc preparation left expanded while the others delegate), no newly created duplicate helper sitting alongside the still-available one, and no re-inlined copy moved into another remaining function.
rubrics.rationale: The five sites absorbed sixteen distinct helpers; the plausible failure mode of this instance is repairing the most visible copies while a reshaped one survives on a side branch or under a new private name.

rubrics.criterion: The caller-specific decisions computed in the commands are preserved and threaded through the restored calls rather than dropped or hardcoded: the activation path still honors the caller's project-directory decision (including the no-cd case) for the working directory and Cmder start variable, and the creation path still installs exactly the requested requirements file and the requested extra packages through the restored delegation.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed code interleaved with caller logic in every site of this instance (argparse results, project directory, installation queue); removing it must not change which inputs reach the restored helper calls.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not achieve delegation by changing the contracts of the still-available helpers in ways their other callers were not updated for: no new required parameters, reordered positional arguments, or altered return-on-error conventions on the process, launch, creation or display helpers used by the remaining commands and the test suite (adding optional parameters with identical defaults is acceptable).
rubrics.rationale: The original helpers stayed live during the growth precisely because other commands and imports still use them; this instance's repair must stay compatible with those callers.

rubrics.criterion: Scaffolding that existed only for the expanded bodies is cleaned up with them: imports that the inlined statements required (for example raw-subprocess symbols or list-arithmetic helpers pulled into the command module) and other module-level additions that only served the copies do not remain behind unused in the touched modules.
rubrics.rationale: The growth pulled module dependencies into the command layer purely to serve the private copies; once the copies return to the helpers, a finished repair leaves no scaffolding whose only purpose was the removed duplication.

rubrics.criterion: No dead residue of the absorbed statements remains inside the repaired functions: unused local variables, temporaries that are created and never used again (such as an rc-file handle no code path reads), or unreachable branches left after the delegation is restored.
rubrics.rationale: The expansions introduced function-local temporaries (rc-file handles, saved-environment snapshots, partial computations) on every site; extracting them is part of a complete repair of this instance.

rubrics.criterion: Environment mutation stays scoped to the child process: launching a subshell or command inside an environment still stages VIRTUAL_ENV/PATH only around the child, still restores the outer process environment afterward (including on launch failure), and still surfaces the same unable-to-find-shell-signature error path. The repair must not leak the staged environment into the parent or lose it on error.
rubrics.rationale: The activation path absorbed a context-managed staging helper and re-expressed it with try/finally; the plausible regression of this instance is restoring the call without the scoping/restore contract.

rubrics.criterion: Creation failure semantics are unchanged: when environment creation or installation fails or is interrupted, the partially created environment is still removed and the failure still propagates instead of exiting cleanly; the clean-up-on-error must not be dropped when the creation steps are delegated.
rubrics.rationale: The instance moved the failure cleanup inline next to the expanded invocation; a delegation-based repair can easily drop the cleanup or swallow the propagating error.

rubrics.criterion: Listing and display output is unchanged in both modes: the same sorted environment order, the same column-count search from the terminal width (including the fallback that never returns zero columns), the same padding and separator arrangement for terminals of any width, and the same space-separated rendering when piped.
rubrics.rationale: Two of the five sites re-derive the column arithmetic; parameter or boundary mistakes when re-delegating (for example passing rows where columns are expected) reproduce only at specific terminal widths, exactly the bug class the original helpers were written to settle.

rubrics.criterion: The import surface of the helper layers is preserved: the existing process/launch/creation/display helper functions keep their names, signatures and module locations, and remain importable exactly as before (the repository test suite imports the display helpers directly; renaming, moving, or re-signaturing them so those imports or calls break fails this item).
rubrics.rationale: This instance deliberately leaves the helpers in place; the repair direction is toward them, not around them, so their disappearance would break third-party consumers of the layering the task asks to restore.

rubrics.criterion: The inspection queries keep their observable semantics: the site-packages location is still obtained by running the environment's own interpreter with the same query, with output decoded and stripped as before, and the no-active-environment case still exits with the same error message and status instead of raising or printing differently.
rubrics.rationale: The inspection site replaced a generic captured-subprocess wrapper with two raw blocks; re-delegating with different stdio wiring, encoding, or stripping changes what users see when inspecting environments.
